keywords: Verification process 2.Problem-solving process 3.Basic skills 4.Data handling skills 5.PBL for science and technology
educationalGoal: -To gain the basic skills needed in processes from finding problems to solutions. -To understand phenomena, objectives, and events quantitatively and qualitatively. -To be able to find characteristics and laws of phenomena, objectives, and events. -To be able to deliver the above information to a third person intelligibly. -To gain various basic skills to proceed smoothly with verification activities. -To be able to have a picture of technology fields and engineers of discipline.
advice: In this course, students will learn the basic skills required for the validation process and problem-solving process in order to achieve the above-mentioned learning and education goals. In addition, this course focuses on the characteristic experiments of the department.One is to learn the basics of “data handling skills” required to collect, organize, analyze, hypothesis test, visualize, and report data. The other is to learn the basic skills of “Science and Engineering PBL”, which includes the basic elements of the process from problem discovery to solution and verification activities. Students learn "data handling skills" and "science and technology PBL" through experiments on basic laws related to electrical and electronic engineering.In “Data Handling Skills”, students acquire and establish knowledge essential for planning, designing, executing, and operating various projects, and learn how to use various measuring instruments. “Science and Engineering PBL (Project Based Learning)” cultivates problem discovery and resolution skills through project issues. The following six project themes will be dealt with, focusing on "Direct Current". (1) Ohm's Law, (2) Power Supplies, (3) Electric Line of Force & Equipotential Lines, (4) Resistors in Series & in Parallel, (5) Kirchhoff's Laws & Superposition Theorem, (6) Joule's Law In order to secure the necessary experiment time, the class will be conducted on the premise of preparation. Always be aware of “safety” during the experiment. In each project, the first week is centered on the acquisition of knowledge and skills necessary for the experiment, and the second week is to tackle the missions using the knowledge and techniques acquired by the team in the first week.
books: Design Project / Introduction of 2025 (Experiment) (Department of Electrical Energy Systems Engineering, Department of Electronics and Information Systems Engineering), Kanazawa Institute of Technology
requiredKnowledge: Each project covers the basic laws and phenomena handled in classes such as "Electric Circuit I" and "Electromagnetics I / II". Challenge the experiment with awareness of the "connection" with these subjects. When collecting information, it is good to use information that suits the purpose of the experiment, such as a Library Center or the Internet. In addition, since reports and posters are created on a personal computer, it is necessary to quickly learn how to use the personal computer and how to use the campus printer.

achievementLevels.ideal: 1) To be able to proceed with activities from problem-finding to solution. 2) To be able to quantitatively and qualitatively recognize phenomena, objects, and events. 3) To be able to recognize characteristics and regularities of corresponding phenomena, objects, and events. 4) To be able to communicate acquired information to a third person intelligibly. 5) To be able to smoothly conduct verification activities independently. 6) To be able to recognize the identity of the major (department) and be proud.
achievementLevels.standard: 1) To be able to proceed with activities from problem-finding to solution with guidance by instructor. 2) To be able to quantitatively and qualitatively recognize phenomena, objects, and events with guidance. 3) To be able to recognize characteristics and regularities of phenomena, objects, and events with guidance. 4) To be able to communicate acquired information to a third person. 5) To be able to conduct verification activities with guidance. 6) To be able to recognize the identity of the major (department) and be proud with guidance.
